messages:
alex: noticed a regression in the short-context path after last night's kernel-autotune rollout. p95 latency for <=64 tokens jumped from 18ms -> 36ms on gpubox-4. anyone else seeing this?
perf-bot: alert: kernel-selector change applied at 2134567200. impacted routes: text.generate (model: rwv1-small). anomaly score: 7.8.
jon: digging in now — grabbed nsys traces on a repro run (short ctx 32 tokens). attaching top-level timeline snippet: 
```
nsys timeline: kernel-launch spikes around 1.2ms, kernel_select_miss count++ at prefetchepoch. periodic fallback to generic-cuda-kernel.
cpu->gpu memcpy wait increased ~0.6ms
```
maria: hmm could be the path-signal threshold we lowered in autotune. we changed the short/long boundary from 80 -> 64 to optimize throughput for 96/128 batched workloads. that might make the selector prefer a kernel optimized for >64 but mis-schedule for true-short.
tara: also check KV cache TTL interplay — if KV hits are cold for short ctx we end up prefill->decode handoff more often which exposes the heavier decode kernel. small requests hit the prefilling heuristics that prefer fused-prefill kernels, but the autotune mapping was biased toward fused-decode for midlength.
jon: quick profiler numbers: 
- baseline (pre-rollout): short path kernel = fused_short_kv (avg 14.5ms total)
- post-rollout pick: generic_decode_opt (avg 28.9ms total)
- observed p50 uplift from 12ms -> 19ms, p95 18ms -> 36ms
looks like mispick.
alex: can we confirm selector logic? where is the seqlen signal coming from — raw token count or smoothed path-signal?
maria: selector reads path_signal = max(raw_len_bucket_score, smoothed_prefill_score). smoothing window = 5s, decay = 0.6. autotune wrote new architecture-aware mapping that prefers arch-optimized kernels when path_signal > 0.4. lowering boundary made many short requests cross 0.4 briefly.
jon: reproduced with unit script: 
```bash
python perf/repro_short.py --model rwv1-small --tokens 32 --rate 200
# observe selector log: path_signal=0.42 -> picked arch_opt_decode
```
perf-bot: telemetry: route=text.generate rwv1-small seqlen=32 path_signal=0.42 kernel=arch_opt_decode kv_hit=true host=gpubox-4
tera: (typo: tara) suggestion: add hysteresis on path_signal transitions rather than hard threshold. e.g. require 3 consecutive samples >0.4 or increase decay so short bursts don't flip picks.
maria: agreed. also propose a quick rollback patch: revert seqlen boundary to 80 for the autotune mapping for this model family until we add hysteresis. can do a canary to 10% traffic.
alex: can we try a quick canary and measure p50/p95? jon can you run the canary job and emit p50/p95 for <=64 bucket?
jon: deploying canary now to gpubox-4 subset (10%). will post numbers in ~10m.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-autotune-seqlen-boundary -> canary(10%) at 2134567895
jon: first 10m window: 
- canary p50 (<=64): 13.2ms vs baseline canary-control 19.1ms
- canary p95 (<=64): 16.8ms vs 35.9ms
looks promising. no regressions for 96/128 observed in this small sample.
tara: long term we should: 
1) add hysteresis on path_signal (3-sample majority + exponential smoothing)
2) instrument per-request selector decision with versioned mapping id
3) add KV-cold flag into selector features so kernel pick accounts for KV warm/cold
4) create automated autotune safety test that runs microbenchmarks for <=64 tokens after mapping changes
maria: I'll open a PR with the revert + telemetry changes. tagging @alex @jon for review.
alex: thanks — schedule follow-up sync if post-canary traffic stays good. good catch everyone :thumbsup:
